notes.meaning: After Moses died, the Lord spoke directly to Joshua to take his place. Joshua had spent many years humbly assisting Moses and learning how to lead. God's plans did not end when His famous servant died, because God had already prepared the next worker.

God told Joshua that because Moses was dead, it was time for him and all the people to get up and cross the Jordan River. A great chapter in Israel's history had closed, but God's work had to move forward. Joshua was called to lead the whole nation into the land God was actively giving them.

The Lord promised that every piece of ground where Israel stepped was already theirs, just as He had told Moses. The land was entirely a gift of God's grace, but the people still had to step out in faith to claim it. God gives His promises freely, yet He calls His people to walk forward and take hold of them.

God described the wide borders of the promised land, stretching from the southern desert to Lebanon in the north, and from the Euphrates River in the east to the Mediterranean Sea in the west. This showed that God was giving Israel a real, physical homeland with clear boundaries. Israel did not fully control all of this vast region until the reigns of King David and King Solomon.

The Lord assured Joshua that no enemy would be able to defeat him as long as he lived. Just as God had been with Moses through every trial, He promised never to leave or abandon Joshua. The secret to real victory was not Joshua's military skill, but the faithful presence of Almighty God.

God commanded Joshua to be strong and courageous because he would lead the people to inherit the land promised to their ancestors. Joshua faced a very difficult task and a nation that had often complained in the past. Remembering that God had sworn a covenant to give them the land gave Joshua the courage he needed to lead.

The Lord told Joshua that true courage meant carefully obeying all the laws given through Moses without turning to the right or to the left. A godly leader needed bravery not only in war, but in standing firm for God's truth every day. Following God's word completely is the true road to wisdom and real success.

Joshua was commanded to speak God's law constantly and think about it day and night so he would be careful to obey everything written in it. Steady study of Scripture keeps God's people from forgetting His commands and falling into sin. When God's word guides our minds and actions, God blesses our path with true wisdom.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some modern teachers use this promise of prosperity to teach that meditating on Scripture guarantees personal financial wealth and worldly success.

notes.meaning: God asked Joshua if He had not already commanded him to be bold and strong, telling him never to be terrified or discouraged. Fear melts away when we realize that God Himself sends us on our mission and walks with us wherever we go. True peace comes from resting in God's power rather than trusting in our own strength.

Joshua acted right away on God's word by giving orders to the officers of the people. These officers were trusted leaders who helped organize the tribes and carry the commander's instructions to the camp. Good leaders rely on faithful helpers to guide God's people smoothly.

The officers told the people to prepare their travel food because they would cross the Jordan in three days to take the land God was giving them. Even though God had miraculously provided manna in the desert, the people now needed to plan ahead and gather ordinary supplies. Faith in God's promises works hand in hand with wise practical preparation.

Joshua spoke specially to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh. These families had chosen to settle in the rich pasture lands on the east side of the Jordan River before Moses died. Joshua now reminded them of the serious promise they had made to help the rest of the nation.

Joshua told these tribes to remember what Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded them. Moses had explained that the Lord had granted them a peaceful home and given them their territory first. When God gives us rest and blessings, we should remember our duty to serve and encourage others.

Their wives, small children, and cattle were allowed to stay safely in the eastern towns that Moses had assigned to them. But their armed fighting men had to march across the river ahead of their brothers to help them conquer Canaan. Those who already enjoy safety must never leave their brothers to fight alone.

The eastern warriors were required to fight until the Lord gave rest to the other tribes and all of Israel received its land. Only after the whole nation had safely inherited its territory could these men return home to enjoy their own properties. God's people share a common bond and must support one another until everyone receives what God promised.

The leaders of the people answered Joshua with complete willingness and loyalty. They promised to do whatever he commanded and to go wherever he sent them on the battlefield. God's people show true unity when they follow their leaders with cheerful and ready hearts.

The people promised to obey Joshua just as they had followed Moses, and they prayed that the Lord would be with him in the same powerful way. They knew that their new leader could only succeed if God remained near him. The best thing believers can do for those in authority is to pray for God's guidance and presence in their work.

The people established strict military order, declaring that anyone who rebelled against Joshua's commands would be put to death. They ended by repeating God's own encouraging words, telling Joshua to be strong and courageous. Hearing his people urge him to take heart gave Joshua great comfort as he began his leadership.
